The results point toward Better Auth for new Next.js SaaS projects, with Clerk and Auth.js as narrower options. Most sources are vendor or SEO blog posts, so treat them as opinion rather than benchmarks.

- **Better Auth:** One 2026 comparison calls it the usual pick for new SaaS apps, mainly because it is a TypeScript-native library that keeps user data in your own Postgres ([makerkit.dev](https://makerkit.dev/blog/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk)). Another credits it with a broad feature set (2FA, passkeys, RBAC, impersonation) through a plugin system, but notes it is newer and leaves security updates to you ([supastarter.dev](https://supastarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-nextauth-vs-clerk)). LogRocket says v1 shipped in early 2025 ([blog.logrocket.com](https://blog.logrocket.com/best-auth-library-nextjs-2026/)).
- **Auth.js (NextAuth v5):** One source describes it as mature and widely used, but says it lacks built-in 2FA, passkeys, or RBAC and that its v5 migration was rough ([supastarter.dev](https://supastarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-nextauth-vs-clerk)). Makerkit calls it a legacy library that teams mostly keep because they already use it. LogRocket says v5 reached stable in late 2024 as a near-complete rewrite.
- **Clerk:** It is a hosted service with prebuilt UI. Critics say costs rise past about 50,000 monthly active users and that user data sits in a US database ([makerkit.dev](https://makerkit.dev/blog/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk)). One pricing table lists a Pro tier at $25/month plus $0.02 per monthly retained user over 50k ([turbostarter.dev](https://www.turbostarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-supabase-auth)). LogRocket reports that Clerk's free tier now covers 50,000 monthly retained users, so check current pricing directly.
- **Supabase Auth:** Makerkit recommends it if you already use Supabase and want Row Level Security to handle part of authorization.

Two cautions. LogRocket notes that many comparison articles were written for Auth.js v4 and older Clerk pricing, so their details may be stale. It also cites CVE-2025-29927, which showed that middleware-only session checks in Next.js can be bypassed, so verify sessions in your route handlers or data layer regardless of which library you choose.

> **Note**: The `middleware` file convention is deprecated and has been renamed to `proxy`. See [Migration to Proxy](#migration-to-proxy) for more details.

The `proxy.js|ts` file is used to write [Proxy](/docs/app/getting-started/proxy) and run code on the server before a request is completed. Then, based on the incoming request, you can modify the response by rewriting, redirecting, modifying the request or response headers, or responding directly.

Proxy executes before routes are rendered. It's particularly useful for implementing custom server-side logic like authentication, logging, or handling redirects.

> **Good to know**:
>
> Proxy is meant to be invoked separately of your render code and in optimized cases deployed to your CDN for fast redirect/rewrite handling, you should not attempt relying on shared modules or globals.
>
> To pass information from Proxy to your application, use [headers](#setting-headers), [cookies](#using-cookies), [rewrites](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response#rewrite), [redirects](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response#redirect), or the URL.

Create a `proxy.ts` (or `.js`) file in the project root, or inside `src` if applicable, so that it is located at the same level as `pages` or `app`.

If you’ve customized [`pageExtensions`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/pageExtensions), for example to `.page.ts` or `.page.js`, name your file `proxy.page.ts` or `proxy.page.js` accordingly.

```tsx filename="proxy.ts" switcher
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'

// This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}

export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
```

```js filename="proxy.js" switcher
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'

// This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside

}

export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
```

## Exports

### Proxy function

The file must export a single function, either as a default export or named `proxy`. Note that multiple proxy from the same file are not supported.

content.text:
Email and password sign-up and sign-in, Google sign-in, and a protected `/dashboard` are all in place. I ran the app locally and checked it with curl. I did not test a real Google login or click through the pages in a browser, because no credentials are set. Nothing is committed.

**What I tested (on a throwaway database, since deleted):**
- A signed-out request to `/dashboard` redirects to `/sign-in?next=/dashboard`.
- Sign-up creates the user and starts a session.
- With that session, the dashboard shows "Signed in as T (t@example.com)".
- A wrong password is rejected.
- Starting Google sign-in produces a valid Google OAuth URL, using the placeholder client ID.
- The `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` pages load.
- Lint passes.
- `tsc` reports one error: `LayoutProps` is not found in `layout.tsx`. That is the scaffold's own file, which I didn't change. I didn't confirm it with `next build`.

**Library choice:** I chose [Better Auth](https://makerkit.dev/blog/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk).
- **Why:** it's a TypeScript-native library that covers email/password and Google, and it keeps user data in our own database. There's no hosted service or per-user pricing.
- **Auth.js (NextAuth v5):** [one comparison](https://supastarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-nextauth-vs-clerk) says it lacks built-in 2FA, passkeys and RBAC, and had a rough v5 migration. Makerkit calls it a legacy library that teams mostly keep because they already use it.
- **Clerk:** it's a hosted service. [Critics](https://makerkit.dev/blog/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk) note costs rise past about 50,000 monthly users and that user data sits in a US database. Pricing figures differ between sources, so check them directly if that matters.
- **Better Auth caveats:** it's newer, and [security updates are your job](https://supastarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-nextauth-vs-clerk).
- **Source quality:** most sources are vendor or SEO posts, so treat the comparison as opinion rather than benchmarks.
- **Storage:** I used a local SQLite file (`better-sqlite3`) so it works with no external service. Swap it for Postgres before deploying anywhere with an ephemeral filesystem, such as serverless hosting.

**How it's wired:**
- **Auth setup:** `src/lib/auth.ts` is the server config, `src/lib/auth-client.ts` is the client, and `src/app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts` is the handler.
- **Protecting `/dashboard`:** `src/proxy.ts` does a quick cookie check, since Next 16 renamed middleware to proxy. The dashboard page also validates the session itself and redirects if it's invalid, because [middleware-only checks have been bypassed before](https://blog.logrocket.com/best-auth-library-nextjs-2026/) (CVE-2025-29927).
- **`src/lib/users.ts`:**
  - `getCurrentUser()` now reads the real session. The old "pick the first user" TODO is gone.
  - `listUsers()` and `getUser()` now read from the auth `user` table.
  - I removed the two hardcoded seed users (Ada and Grace), because they had no passwords and couldn't sign in.
- **Pages:** `/sign-in` and `/sign-up` share one form with a "Continue with Google" button. The `?next=` redirect only accepts same-site paths. The dashboard has a sign-out button.
- **Config:**
  - `.env.example` holds placeholders for the session secret, the app URL, the Google client ID and secret, and the database path.
  - `.gitignore` now keeps `.env.example` tracked and ignores `/data/`.

**To use it:**
1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and set a real `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` (`openssl rand -base64 32`).
2. Create a Google OAuth client with redirect URI `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google`, and fill in the client ID and secret.
3. Run `npm run auth:migrate` once to create the tables. It's a new script I added to `package.json`.

Email verification and password reset aren't set up. They need an email provider, so I left them out.

Sources:
- [Better Auth vs Clerk vs NextAuth vs Supabase Auth (Makerkit)](https://makerkit.dev/blog/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk)
- [better-auth vs NextAuth vs Clerk (Supastarter)](https://supastarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-nextauth-vs-clerk)
- [Best auth library for Next.js 2026 (LogRocket)](https://blog.logrocket.com/best-auth-library-nextjs-2026/)
- [Better Auth vs Clerk vs NextAuth vs Supabase Auth (TurboStarter)](https://www.turbostarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-supabase-auth)
